Stage 1 — Property Planning Score
How to use:
1. Select the property to plan
2. Load its previous audit report (.docx)
3. Select the Property Complexity bands
4. Click Calculate Property Planning Score

The system extracts sensitivity distribution and outstanding observations from the uploaded report and computes a risk-based priority tier.

📄 Databank Manager
Browse, edit, suppress and merge observations in the audit databank. All changes are stored locally and reversible.
📄 Databank Manager — User Guide
Basic Actions
Click any rowOpens the observation detail panel on the right in read-only view. Read the full observation text and recommendation before taking any action.
✏ Edit DetailsSwitches to edit mode. You can update the title, category, type, observation text and recommendation. Changes are saved to your local browser and do not affect other users.
🔴 SuppressHides the observation from all filters, searches and reports without permanently deleting it. It can be restored at any time using the Suppressed filter.
🟢 RestoreBrings a suppressed observation back to active status. Use the Suppressed only filter to find suppressed observations.
⇄ MergeSuppresses one observation and keeps the other as the canonical version. Use when two observations have the same meaning but different wording.
↩ Undo LastReverses the most recent action (suppress, restore, edit or merge). Up to 50 actions can be undone within the current session.
🔍 Scan DuplicatesAutomatically scans all active observations and finds pairs with 70%+ title similarity. Both observations are shown side by side in full so you can read and compare before deciding which to keep.
🔒 HO Update Workflow (step by step)
1 Auditor makes changes in Databank Manager (suppress, edit or merge observations), then clicks "📤 Export Proposed Changes". This downloads a small dbm-proposed-changes.json file and sends it to HO. 2 Administrator opens the system, goes to Databank Manager, and clicks "🔒 Import & Review (HO)" (requires Administrator password). A review screen opens showing every proposed change with Approve / Reject checkboxes. 3 HO reviews each change, ticks or unticks as required, then clicks "Apply Approved Changes". The approved changes are now active in HO's browser session. 4 HO clicks "🔒 Update HTML File". This permanently bakes all approved changes into a new file called index-updated.html which is saved to the Downloads folder on HO's computer. 5 HO renames index-updated.html to index.html and uploads it to Netlify. All auditors who open the Netlify link will now have the updated databank automatically.
Important Notes
• All changes made in Databank Manager are saved in the browser only — they are not written into the HTML file automatically.
• The dbm-proposed-changes.json file exported by an auditor is not a system file and cannot be uploaded to Netlify directly.
• Only the index-updated.html produced by "Update HTML File" should be uploaded to Netlify.
• After uploading to Netlify, ask auditors to do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) once to ensure they get the latest version.
